subject: KEK lattice escrow & failover playbook — design questions and runbook draft
messages:
From: Jared Klein <jared.klein@northbridge.io>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Moss <cmoss@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: KEK escrow + automatic failover — quick clarifying questions

Nikhil,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment options yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our security team about the KEK (key-encryption-key) "lattice" escrow approach you mentioned:

- If our HSM cluster becomes unreachable, what triggers the escrow extraction flow? Is it purely operator-initiated or can it be automated by healthchecks?
- During escrow unlock, which operations are allowed on the served models (read-only inference vs. model re-writes)?
- What audit evidence is generated during escrow/unseal events (signed attestations, logs, timestamped artifacts)?

We are collecting these answers for our compliance packet (SOC2 + internal audit). If you have a short runbook or a diagram, that would be extremely helpful.

-Jared
Jared Klein
Head of Cloud Security, Northbridge Systems
[jared.klein@northbridge.io]

Attachment: none
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Klein <jared.klein@northbridge.io>
Cc: Claire Moss <cmoss@acme-corp.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: KEK escrow + automatic failover — quick clarifying questions

Jared — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, expanded below and attaching a draft diagram + playbook.

1) Triggering escrow extraction: operator-initiated by default; optional auto-trigger via configurable health-policy (we recommend manual escalation + automated pre-checks).
2) Allowed operations during escrow/unseal: read-only inference only; writes (model uploads, key rotations that produce new KEKs) are blocked until normal mode is restored.
3) Audit evidence: HSM-signed event, KMS audit entry, prefix/KV cache snapshot marker, and a signed runbook checkpoint artifact uploaded to your SIEM/DR bucket.

Attached: kek-lattice-escrow-architecture-v1.pdf, escrow-failover-playbook-draft.xlsx

I'll also loop in Mina (ops lead) to review the operator checks and Soojin on the operator-eviction safeguards.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: FW: KEK escrow + automatic failover — quick clarifying questions

Team — forwarding Northbridge's questions and the draft playbook I just sent. Need a technical sanity check before we send final wording to Jared. Key things to validate:

- "Auto-trigger" options: The doc proposes a health policy that can automatically start the escrow pre-check (not the final extraction) after N failed control-plane heartbeats. We say final extraction requires operator confirmation and two-person auth. Is that correct?
- Read-only during escrow: do we have any preexisting failure cases where writes might be needed (e.g., emergency patch that updates inference runtime)? If so, how do we permit it safely?
- Audit artifact format: current proposal is HSM-signed JSON certificate + SHA256 of unsealed-key blob, pushed to S3 with object-lock. Any missing pieces?

Please reply inline. I want to close this by EOD Monday so they can include it in their compliance packet.

Thanks,
Nikhil

Nikhil / team — quick notes inline: 

- Auto-trigger: agree with manual final confirmation. Add: auto-pre-check should only collect evidence (HSM health, node liveness, network partition status) and create a tamper-evident pre-check bundle. Don't allow any key material movement during pre-check.
- Two-person auth: recommend operator + CSO-approved delegate or a signed ticket from the customer's ticketing system (DocuSign-style binding for emergency processes).
- Read-only: we must allow a constrained maintenance window for hotfixes, but only if a separate ephemeral administrative key is provisioned that is itself escrow-protected. Document that as an exceptional flow.
- Audit artifact: add signed attestation from the operator machine (TPM quote) and a proof-of-possession record for the KEK fragment shards. Use object-lock + WORM retention.

I'll update the playbook spreadsheet with these rows and flag the exceptional hotfix path for legal to bless.

—Soojin

Subject: Re: FW: KEK escrow + automatic failover — quick clarifying questions

Quick from me — added comments in the attached playbook where we need more precise knobs and failure thresholds. Highlights:

- Health policy: set pre-check trigger to 3 consecutive control-plane RPC failures across >50% of leadership nodes OR explicit operator report from all-region monitoring.
- Extraction workflow: require 2-of-3 operator approvals (region owner + onsite ops + remote ops). If remote ops is unavailable, require signed emergency ticket and a 30-minute quorum timer before extraction is allowed.
- Hotfix exception: create ephemeral admin key that is split into 3 shards; unsealing ephemeral key requires same 2-of-3 but is allowed only for a single signed package deployment. Record package SHA and block further admin key reuse until rotation.
- Evidence: HSM-signed attestation, operator TPM quote, system snapshot (KV prefix hash), upload to customer-locked S3 with object-lock. Add a compact human-readable summary (PDF) for auditors.

I'll tidy the spreadsheet and send back to Nikhil for external delivery. Recommend we call Jared tomorrow to walk through the flow.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Final: KEK lattice escrow + failover playbook (draft) — answers and next steps

Jared / Claire — attaching the revised playbook and diagram per our internal review. Summary of decisions: 

- Escrow triggering: pre-check auto-run allowed (collect-only); final extraction requires 2-of-3 operator approvals OR operator + signed emergency ticket after a 30-minute quorum wait.
- Mode during escrow/unseal: read-only inference only. An exceptional hotfix path exists using an ephemeral admin key (3-shard split) allowed for a single signed package deployment; this path is logged and forces immediate rotation.
- Audit evidence: HSM-signed attestation, operator TPM quote, KV-prefix snapshot hash, and a signed human-readable summary document. All artifacts uploaded to customer-controlled object-lock S3 with WORM retention.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm Northbridge is comfortable with the 2-of-3 operator model and the emergency-ticket fallback.
2) If OK, we can co-schedule a 30-minute walkthrough (we suggest Tue 22 Jun or Wed 23 Jun).
3) We'll update the final playbook with your legal team's wording for the hotfix exception.

Attached: kek-lattice-escrow-architecture-v1.pdf (revised), escrow-failover-playbook-draft.xlsx (with operations comments)

Thanks for the quick review cycle — let us know which time works for the walkthrough.

—Nikhil
